item.title: Reshaping Organisations and Supply Chains in a Polycrisis Era: Interdependent Climate, Geopolitical, Economic and Technological Shocks
item.content:encoded:
This is a special joint initiative between the British Journal of Management and the International Journal of Operations & Production Management, focusing on how organisations and supply chains are being reshaped in response to interconnected polycrisis challenges involving climate, geopolitical, economic, and technological shocks.

item.title: Imagining Post-growth
item.content:encoded:
Fred Basso, London School of Economics and Political Science

Nil Özçağlar-Toulouse, Université de Lille

Julien Troiville, ESG Université du Québec À Montréal

This special issue addresses the urgent need to rethink marketing's role in a post-growth future. With humanity facing catastrophic climate change caused primarily by human activity, marketing must shift from promoting unlimited consumption to supporting genuinely sustainable lifestyles. Post-growth, increasingly studied across environmental sciences, economics, and social sciences, challenges societies' dependence on economic growth and questions the link between prosperity and consumerism.

The special issue seeks contributions exploring three interconnected questions: how marketing can challenge growth-oriented systems and critique its own pro-growth practices; how marketing can support degrowth transitions and transform economic practices; and how marketing can function within a post-growth economy while meeting human needs within planetary boundaries. Contributions should bridge theory and practice, examining tensions between individual and systemic responsibility, alternative practices, and marketing's evolving role.

Appel publié par Recherche et Applications en Marketing (French Edition). Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How marketing can challenge the status quo and question growth-oriented practices, including the critique of desire creation, ethical marketing practices, and the individualization of consumer responsibility
  • How marketing can engage in degrowth practices and implement transformative strategies, including conceptual clarification of degrowth-related concepts and reinventing marketing practices and education
  • How a post-growth economy can be maintained, including the transition from unlimited desires to meeting human needs within consumption corridors and the role of marketing in supporting sufficient lifestyles
  • Critical examination of marketing's role in climate change and planetary boundaries, questioning the relationship between prosperity, productivism, and economic growth
  • Marketing education and pedagogy in the context of post-growth transitions, including decolonial and indigenous perspectives
  • Empirical and conceptual research addressing post-growth marketing from various theoretical, methodological, and disciplinary angles
  • Research in non-WEIRD contexts and with decolonial and indigenous perspectives

Timeline

  • May 1, 2026: Submission platform opens
  • July 1, 2026: Special issue publication date
  • January 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Wildfires in a Changing Climate: Impacts, Adaptation, and Policy
item.content:encoded:
Sarah Meier, ETH Zurich

Eric Strobl, University of Bern

Robert J. R. Elliott, University of Birmingham

Wildfires are becoming more frequent and intense in many regions, driven by climate change, land-use shifts, and expanding human settlements in fire-prone areas. These changes have transformed wildfires into systemic economic and ecological risks. The economic impacts are substantial and multifaceted, extending beyond direct suppression costs to include disruptions to supply chains, labour productivity losses, effects on tourism and housing markets, and significant public health burdens from smoke exposure.

This special issue seeks empirical research that quantifies the economic consequences of wildfires and smoke, and evaluates the effectiveness of policy responses and adaptation strategies. The journal welcomes applied environmental and resource economics studies using innovative data sources and identification methods, as well as interdisciplinary work that strengthens economic understanding of wildfire impacts and informs policy decisions. The issue particularly encourages cross-regional comparisons to facilitate knowledge exchange between regions with established fire experience and those facing emerging vulnerabilities.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Labour productivity, sectoral employment shifts, and worker mobility
  • Housing markets, mortgage risk, and migration and other behavioural responses to wildfire risk and exposure
  • Natural capital and ecosystem service valuation, including impacts on biodiversity, recreation, and forest asset pricing
  • Inequality, information access, and distributional impacts of exposure and monitoring technologies
  • Public finance, insurance markets, and the fiscal consequences for local and regional governments
  • Institutions, governance, and risk-sharing arrangements, including coordination across jurisdictions, public-private roles, and firm responses to wildfire risk
  • Prevention, suppression, and adaptation strategies, including land-use planning, prescribed burning, indigenous fire stewardship, and advanced monitoring and management technologies
  • Welfare losses from smoke exposure, including physical and mental health outcomes and associated human capital effects

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Submission deadline
